q: 1. When was the Civil Service Act introduced in Nepal for the first time?
explain: The first Civil Service Act of Nepal was promulgated on Bhadra 22, 2013 B.S. during the premiership of Tanka Prasad Acharya.

q: 2. In which year, M.N. Booch commission on administration reform was constituted in Nepal?
explain: The M.N. Booch Commission was formed in 2009 B.S. to provide recommendations for administrative restructuring following the end of the Rana regime.

q: 3. Civil service Act in Nepal, was introduced under the leadership of prime minister of -----
explain: Tanka Prasad Acharya is credited with introducing the Civil Service Act in 2013 B.S., which organized the civil service for the first time.

q: 4. Under whose leadership was the High level Administrative Reform Commission, 2048 constituted?
explain: The High-level Administrative Reform Commission (2048) was chaired by then-Prime Minister Girija Prasad Koirala to modernize the administration.

q: 5. The Government of Nepal has started celebrating civil service day since;
explain: Civil Service Day has been celebrated annually on Bhadra 22 since 2061 B.S. to commemorate the enactment of the first Civil Service Act.

q: 6. From which amendment of civil service act has the provision to make civil service inclusive begun?
options: The provision was there from beginning
explain: The Second Amendment of the Civil Service Act (2064 B.S.) introduced the reservation system to make the service more inclusive.

q: 7. Public service commission was established in:
explain: The Public Service Commission (Lok Sewa Aayog) was established on Ashadh 1, 2008 B.S.

q: 8. Which country started the concept of civil service competition for the first time?
explain: China is historically recognized as the first country to implement a competitive merit-based system for civil service recruitment.

q: 9. Since, when the Civil Service Act, 2049 came into effect?
explain: The current Civil Service Act, 2049, officially came into effect on 2050/02/04 B.S.

q: 10. How many chapters and sections are there in the civil service Act - 2049?
explain: The Civil Service Act, 2049 contains 10 Chapters and 76 Sections (including several amended/added clauses).

q: 11. How many times has the Civil Service Act - 2049, been amended so far?
explain: The Civil Service Act, 2049 has undergone four significant amendments to date.

q: 12. In which part of the Constitution of Nepal is Public service commission incorporated?
explain: Provisions regarding the Public Service Commission are located in Part 23 of the current Constitution of Nepal.

q: 13. In which article of the constitution of Nepal, the formation of the Government Civil Service system is included?
explain: Article 285 of the Constitution of Nepal provides for the formation of the Government Civil Service and other government services.

q: 14. Reservation for the scheduled castes and scheduled tribes in the public services has been provided in the present Constitution of Nepal under --------
explain: Article 285 (2) specifies that positions in the Federal Civil Service and other Federal Government Services shall be filled through open competition on the basis of the principle of inclusion.

q: 15. According to the Civil Service Act, 2049, 'Permanent post' means, a post of the civil service which is;
options: of which term is not specified
explain: A permanent post is defined as a pensionable post of the Civil Service for which no time limit is fixed.

q: 16. How many types of civil service have provisioned in Civil Service Act- 2049?
explain: The Act categorizes the Civil Service into 10 services (Administrative, Engineering, Forest, etc.).

q: 17. According to the Civil Service Act, 2049 and the Civil Service Rules, 2050, how many groups are there under the Nepal Administrative Service?
explain: Nepal Administrative Service consists of 3 groups: General Administration, Revenue, and Accounts.

q: 18. How many groups are formed under the Nepal Engineering Service as per the Civil Service Rules, 2050?
explain: As per current rules, there are 15 distinct groups under the Nepal Engineering Service (Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, etc.).

q: 19. Under which ministry does the operational jurisdiction of the General Sub-group of the Civil Engineering Group in the Nepal Engineering Service fall?
options: Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration
Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport
Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation
explain: The Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport serves as the lead ministry for the Civil Engineering General sub-group.

q: 20. How many Classes of Gazette Officer have been provisioned by the Civil service Act 2049 of Nepal?
explain: Gazetted officers are divided into 3 classes: Third, Second,  First and the Special Class).

q: 21. How many times has the civil service rules been amended so far?
explain: The Civil Service Rules (2050) have been amended 15 times to accommodate administrative changes.

q: 22. How many classes are there in non-gazette level of civil service of Nepal?
explain: The non-gazetted level includes 5 classes: First, Second, Third, Fourth, and the unclassified (shreni-bihin) category.

q: 23. Which section of the Civil service Act, 2049 has provisioned about fulfillment of Vacancy in Civil service under the three chapters?
explain: Section 7 of the Civil Service Act, 2049 details the procedures and percentages for filling vacant posts.

q: 24. According to civil service Act-2049, what percent of allocation has been made for gazette third class in the free competition?
explain: For Gazetted Third Class, 70% of posts are filled through open (free) competition.

q: 25. According to civil service Act - 2049, what percent of allocation has been made for non-gazette first class in the open competition?
explain: For Non-Gazetted First Class (Nayab Subba), 40% of posts are allocated for open competition.

q: 26. What percent of the total vacant post are recruited by open competition in the non-gazette first class level of civil service of Nepal?
explain: Similar to question 25, 40% is the fixed percentage for open recruitment at the Non-Gazetted First Class level.

q: 27. According to Civil Service Act- 2049, what percent of allocation has been made for non-gazette second class in the free competition?
explain: For Non-Gazetted Second Class (Kharidar), 70% of posts are filled through free competition.

q: 28. According to Civil Service Act- 2049, what percentage of reservation in Civil service in Nepal should be made during recruitment of staff in the free competition?
explain: Out of the total open competition seats, 45% are reserved for various inclusive categories (Women, Dalit, etc.).

q: 29. According to civil service Act - 2049, what percent of allocation has been made for gazette first class in the free competition?
explain: For Gazetted First Class (Sahayak Sachiv/Under Secretary), only 10% are recruited via open competition.

q: 30. Match the following as per the provision of reservation (Backward region, Disabled, Dalits, Madhesi):
explain: The 45% reservation is split: Women (33%), Adibasi Janajati (27%), Madhesi (22%), Dalit (9%), Disabled (5%), and Backward area (4%).

q: 31. How many districts has the Civil Service Act -2049, covered under 'backward area'?
explain: There are 9 districts defined as backward areas (Achham, Kalikot, Jajarkot, Jumla, Dolpa, Bajhang, Bajura, Mugu, and Humla).

q: 32. Which district doesn't belong to Backward Area?
explain: Rukum is not listed among the 9 specific districts designated as 'Backward Area' under the Civil Service Act.

q: 33. Which section of the Civil service Act-2049, has provisioned about disqualifications for being candidate under chapter three?
explain: Section 10 of the Act lists the reasons an individual might be disqualified from joining the civil service.

q: 34. The minimum age required for entering into gazette post of government of Nepal is;
explain: To apply for a Gazetted post, the candidate must have attained the age of 21 years.

q: 35. Within how many days must the appointing authority issue the appointment letter for Non-Gazetted posts after recommendation?
explain: The appointing authority must issue the appointment letter within 15 days of the recommendation.

q: 36. For how long is the probation period for a new permanent employee in Civil Service?
options: 1 year for men and 6 months for women
explain: The probation period is 1 year for male employees and 6 months for female employees.

q: 37. According to Civil Service Act-2049, the tenure of the Chief Secretary of Nepal is ------
explain: The Chief Secretary of the Government of Nepal has a fixed tenure of 3 years.

q: 38. According to Civil Service Act -2049, what is the age limitation for the retirement of a civil servant in Nepal?
explain: Currently, the age of mandatory retirement for civil servants in Nepal is 58 years.

q: 39. In how much percentage of posts is there a provision for promotion through performance evaluation?
explain: Generally, 40% of the vacant posts for certain higher levels are filled via promotion based on performance evaluation.

q: 40. What is the maximum number of marks that can be obtained for seniority for promotion?
explain: In the promotion scoring system, a maximum of 30 marks is allocated for seniority.

q: 41. According to the Civil Service Rules 2050, how many marks are provided for service in geographical region?
explain: A total of 16 marks is allocated for work experience in different geographical regions (A, B, C, D).

q: 42. Maximum evaluation mark that may be granted by the supervisor?
explain: In performance evaluation, the supervisor can award a maximum of 25 marks.

q: 43. The registration of the trade union of civil employees shall be made in the -------
options: Department of labour and employment promotion
Ministry of federal affairs and general administration
explain: The Department of Labour and Employment Promotion is responsible for the registration of civil employee trade unions.

q: 44. Correct statement: I. First amendment provided Trade Union rights. II. Second amendment provisioned for reservation.
explain: Both statements are historically correct regarding the development of the Civil Service Act.

q: 45. Which section provisioned 'professional organization of civil employees'?
explain: Section 53 of the Civil Service Act, 2049 contains provisions relating to professional organizations.

q: 46. From which amendment are civil servants prohibited from acquiring foreign permanent residency (DV/PR)?
explain: The Fourth Amendment explicitly prohibited civil servants from holding or applying for foreign permanent residency.

q: 47. Which chapter of the Civil Service Act -2049, has provisioned about the code of conduct?
explain: Chapter 7 (Sections 41 to 55) details the 'Conduct' or code of behavior for civil servants.

q: 48. Which section provisioned about the restriction on criticizing government?
explain: Section 45 restricts civil servants from making public criticisms of the government.

q: 49. Which section has provisioned about the 'Statement of property'?
explain: Section 54 requires civil servants to submit an annual statement of their property/assets.

q: 50. 'No civil employee shall subject any one to torture', which section deals with this?
explain: Section 54 (a) was added to ensure civil servants do not engage in or subject others to torture.

q: 51. Which of the following punishment is not included in the ordinary punishments that may be subjected to the departmental punishments to the employees of Civil Service?
options: Withholding of promotion for two years or withholding of two salary increments
Withholding of two to five salary increments
Removal from service, without being disqualified for government service in the future.
explain: Ordinary punishments include censure and withholding increments/promotions. Removal from service is categorized as a 'Special Punishment' under the Civil Service Act.

q: 52. In which of the following circumstances, a civil employee may be removed from service, without being disqualified for government service in the future if he/she?
options: frequently violates the matters relating to conduct
explain: According to Section 61, repeated indiscipline, political participation, and conduct violations are all grounds for removal without future disqualification.

q: 53. Which of following punishment is subjected to a civil employee, if his/her performance didn't found satisfactory?
options: withholding of promotion for upto two years
withholding of a maximum of two salary increments
explain: Poor performance or failing to meet job responsibilities can result in any of these ordinary departmental punishments.

q: 54. In which of the following circumstances, a civil employee may be dismissed from service, with being disqualified for government service in the future, if he/she?
options: convicted by a court of a criminal offence involving moral turpitude
obtain or apply for a permanent residence permit
explain: Dismissal with disqualification is the most severe penalty, reserved for crimes involving moral turpitude, corruption, or holding foreign PR/DV.

q: 55. According to the Civil Service Act 2049, leave is merely; a/an:
explain: The Act explicitly states that leave is a privilege and not a right; the authority can refuse or cancel leave based on the exigency of work.

q: 56. How many types of leave are provided under the Civil Service Act, 2049?
explain: There are 9 types of leave: Casual, Festival, Home, Sick, Maternity/Maternity Care, Study, Extraordinary, Substitution, and Paternity leave.

q: 57. According to Civil Service Rules 2050, there is a provision that employees can get festival leave without increasing it by ------- days throughout the year.
explain: Civil servants are granted 6 days of casual leave and 6 days of festival leave (total 12) per year.

q: 58. What does a suspended employee get during the period of suspension from the regular job, as per to Civil Service Act, 2049?
options: Half of the salary amount and festival allowance
Half of the salary amount and half of the festival allowance
One fourth of the salary amount and festival allowance
explain: During suspension, an employee is only entitled to half of their basic salary to meet subsistence needs.

q: 59. According to Civil Service Rules-2050, how many days civil servant can get sick leave per year?
explain: A civil servant is entitled to 12 days of fully paid sick leave every year.

q: 60. According to Civil Service Rules 2050, In cases where a female civil employee becomes pregnant, how many days of maternity leave is there?
explain: Following the latest amendments to align with labor laws, maternity leave has been extended to 98 days.

q: 61. According to the civil service rules, if the wife of a male civil servant gives birth, how many days of maternity care leave?
explain: A male civil servant is entitled to 15 days of maternity care (paternity) leave to look after his wife and newborn.

q: 62. According to Civil Service Rules 2050, how many days can an employee accumulate the vacation leave he/she has earned?
explain: Home leave can be accumulated up to a maximum of 180 days throughout the service period.

q: 63. According to Civil Service Act-2049, which of the following leave can get by Civil servants?
explain: Festival, Home, and Study leaves are all standard provisions defined within the Act and Rules.

q: 64. How many years of permanent service period should an employee has completed to get study leave?
explain: A civil servant must complete at least 3 years of permanent service to become eligible for study leave.

q: 65. Which of the following leave is not available to an employee of the Civil Service?
explain: 'Visit leave' is not a recognized category of leave under the Nepal Civil Service Rules.

q: 66. Who approves the extraordinary leave of a civil servant?
explain: Because extraordinary leave is for a long duration (up to 3 years or 5 total), it must be approved by the Government of Nepal (Council of Ministers).

q: 67. Which ministry acts as the central body for the management and operation of civil service and employees?
options: Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration
explain: The Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration (MoFAGA) is the central personnel agency of the Government of Nepal.
